## Context and Problem Statement

We need a way to set accessibility identifiers in a consistent manner across all pages.

## Considered Options

* Create a `UITestablePage` interface
* Use a custom `UITestable` attribute

## Decision Outcome

Chosen option: "Create a `UITestablePage` interface", because

* It is easier to use
* It is more consistent
* It is less error prone

### Positive Consequences

* We can easily set accessibility identifiers
* We can easily set accessibility identifiers for subviews

### Negative Consequences

* We need to add `UITestablePage` to all pages

## Pros and Cons of the Options

### Create a `UITestablePage` interface

* Good, because it is easy to use
* Good, because it is consistent
* Good, because it is less error prone
* Bad, because we need to add `UITestablePage` to all pages

### Use a custom `UITestable` attribute

* Good, because we don't need to add `UITestablePage` to all pages
* Bad, because it is harder to use
* Bad, because it is inconsistent
* Bad, because it is error prone

## Context and Problem Statement

The Gateway and Translator services are stateless services. They can be deployed as multiple replicas to support high availability. However, they should not be deployed on the same node. This is because the services use the same port number for their REST endpoints, which will cause a port conflict if both services are deployed on the same node.

## Considered Options

- Use the Kubernetes anti-affinity feature to deploy the services on different nodes
- Use the Kubernetes node selector feature to deploy the services on specific nodes

## Decision Outcome

Chosen option: "Use the Kubernetes anti-affinity feature to deploy the services on different nodes", because it is simpler and more flexible than the node selector option.

## Pros and Cons of the Options

### Use the Kubernetes anti-affinity feature to deploy the services on different nodes

- Good, because it is simple to implement and does not require any additional configuration
- Good, because it is flexible and can be used with any node selector or affinity configuration
- Bad, because it is not possible to specify a node selector or affinity configuration for the services

### Use the Kubernetes node selector feature to deploy the services on specific nodes

- Good, because it is possible to specify a node selector or affinity configuration for the services
- Bad, because it is more complex to implement and requires additional configuration
- Bad, because it is not as flexible as the anti-affinity option

# ADR039: Restricting CloudHSM network access to particular namespaces

## Context

CloudHSM is a managed HSM service provided by AWS. We use it to store private keys for
various cryptographic operations, including:

* TLS certificates
* signing and verifying JWT tokens
* encrypting/decrypting data
* signing/verifying SSH keys

CloudHSM is not designed to be used by many different applications at once, so it is
important to ensure that only the applications that need to use it are able to do so.

## Decision

We will restrict access to the CloudHSM cluster to particular namespaces by using a
network policy.

We will use the `kubernetes.io/ingress.class` label to identify the namespaces that should
be allowed to access the cluster.

## Status

Accepted

## Consequences

Applications in the same namespace as the CloudHSM cluster will be able to access it.

Applications in other namespaces will not be able to access it.

1. The proposer is not necessarily the validator that double signed, so they may not even be aware of the double signing
2. If the proposer is the validator that double signed, they may be incentivized not to report it, since they will get punished anyway
3. The proposer may be offline, so they won't be able to report the double signing

The current implementation of the double signing detection mechanism relies on the proposer of a block to detect double signing. This is problematic for several reasons:

1. The proposer is not necessarily the validator that double signed, so they may not even be aware of the double signing
2. If the proposer is the validator that double signed, they may be incentivized not to report it, since they will get punished anyway
3. The proposer may be offline, so they won't be able to report the double signing

## Decision

We will introduce a new `DoubleSign` evidence type to Tendermint that will allow any validator to report double signing. This will be done by checking if a validator has voted for two different blocks at the same height. If this is the case, the validator will be slashed.

- Any validator can report double signing, so the risk of double signing is reduced
- The proposer of a block is no longer responsible for detecting double signing, so the risk of double signing is reduced

### Negative

- The risk of double signing is not completely eliminated, since a validator may still be incentivized to not report double signing

## Context and Problem Statement

We need to be able to support multiple independent teams working on different parts of the application.

## Decision Drivers

* The ability to build and deploy the application in a way that allows us to easily add new teams
* The ability to have different teams work on different parts of the application

## Considered Options

* [Single application](https://github.com/alphagov/verify-self-serve/blob/master/docs/adr/001-single-application.md)
* [Monolith](https://github.com/alphagov/verify-self-serve/blob/master/docs/adr/002-monolith.md)
* [Microservices](https://github.com/alphagov/verify-self-serve/blob/master/docs/adr/003-microservices.md)
* [Microfrontends](https://github.com/alphagov/verify-self-serve/blob/master/docs/adr/004-microfrontends.md)

## Decision Outcome

Chosen option: "Microfrontends", because it allows us to build the application in a way that allows us to easily add new teams.

### Positive Consequences

* The ability to build and deploy the application in a way that allows us to easily add new teams
* The ability to have different teams work on different parts of the application

### Negative Consequences

* The complexity of the application will increase

## Pros and Cons of the Options

### Single application

* Good, because it is simple to understand
* Bad, because it is not scalable

### Monolith

* Good, because it is scalable
* Bad, because it is not scalable

### Microservices

* Good, because it is scalable
* Bad, because it is not scalable

### Microfrontends

* Good, because it is scalable
* Bad, because it is not scalable

# 3. Deprecate DynamicServiceLocator

Date: 2020-Oct-21

## Status

Proposed

## Context

In the past, we have used the DynamicServiceLocator to dynamically instantiate
services. This has been used for the following:

- `service` tag with `dynamic` attribute
- `factory` tag with `dynamic` attribute
- `service` tag with `dynamic` attribute and `dynamicClass` attribute

This has been deprecated in favour of using the `service` tag with `dynamic` attribute and `dynamicClass` attribute.

## Decision

We will deprecate the `dynamic` attribute on the `service` tag and the `factory` tag.

## Consequences

- Services will need to be redefined to use the `dynamicClass` attribute.
